title: Maya call script
transcriptText:
Hey, this is Maya from Northstar Revenue. I know this is out of the blue, so I’ll be quick. I’m calling because your team posted three AE roles last week, and I also noticed you’re hiring for sales enablement. Usually when those two things happen together, someone is trying to ramp reps faster without making managers listen to every call manually. Is that close?

That makes sense. The reason I thought this might be relevant is that we help revenue teams turn sales calls into coaching moments automatically. Not just summaries, but where the buyer got confused, where trust improved, where the rep over-explained, and where the next step became easier or harder.

Can I ask how call coaching works today? Is it mostly manager shadowing, scorecards, Gong snippets, or just pipeline outcomes showing up later?

Got it. So you have recordings, but the review process depends heavily on each manager. That is exactly the gap we usually see. The problem is not lack of data. It is that nobody has time to turn all those calls into consistent coaching.

Where we fit is simple. We analyze recent calls and give managers a weekly coaching map: which reps are struggling with discovery, which calls created too much effort for the buyer, which objections were handled well, and which three-minute moments are worth reviewing with the team.

This would not replace your call recording system. It sits on top of it. Think of it as the layer that turns raw conversation data into manager-ready coaching.

The useful next step is not a big demo. I’d suggest a twenty-five minute working session. Bring one anonymized discovery call, and we’ll show you what the coaching output would look like. If it feels generic, we stop there. If it finds real coaching moments, then we can talk about a small pilot.

I have Wednesday at 2:00 Eastern or Thursday at 11:00. Wednesday works? Perfect. I’ll send a tight invite with one example call, what the model sees, and what a two-week pilot would require.
